adolf-zeising.name: Zeising, Adolf
adolf-zeising.bio: Author of Neue Lehre von den Proportionen des menschlichen Körpers (Leipzig, 1854), which sought to establish the Golden Section as the universal morphological law of the human body, nature, and classical art; discussed by Winterberg in the Einleitung (fn. 4).

adolphe-quetelet.name: Quetelet, Adolphe
adolphe-quetelet.role: Belgian Astronomer, Mathematician, and Founder of Anthropometry

works: Anthropométrie, ou Mesure des différentes facultés de l'homme (1870)

albert-ilg.name: Ilg, Albert
albert-ilg.role: Austrian Art Historian and Editor of Quellenschriften (Neue Folge)
albert-ilg.bio: Director at the Kunsthistorisches Museum in Vienna who succeeded Rudolf von Eitelberger as general editor of the Neue Folge of Quellenschriften für Kunstgeschichte und Kunsttechnik, in which Winterberg's 1889 edition of Pacioli appeared as Band II.

carl-schmidt.bio: Author of Proportionsschlüssel: Neues System der Verhältnisse des menschlichen Körpers (Stuttgart, 1849), which modified Carus's vertebral module to include the cranial bones for measuring the extremities; cited by Winterberg in the Einleitung.

catano-catani.role: Merchant of Borgo Sansepolcro in Florence
catano-catani.bio: Compatriot of Luca Pacioli with whom Pacioli visited the Villa del Tovaglia outside Florence (Architectura Cap. VIII).

chalcidius.role: Late Antique Translator and Commentator on Plato's Timaeus

prosdocimo-beldomandi.bio: Professor of Astrology and Mathematics at the University of Padua, cited by Pacioli ('Prodocimo') in Compendio Chapter II alongside Ptolemy, Albumasar, and Bianchini.

ptolemy.name: Ptolemy, Claudius
ptolemy.bio: Author of the Almagest and Cosmographia (Geography); cited by Pacioli on the chord of the pentagon and hexadecagon, spherical astronomy, and cartographic scaling.

san-rocco.bio: Venerated in Venice at the Church and Scuola Grande di San Rocco; glossed by Winterberg in the Dedication of the Tractato de l'Architectura (fn. 1).

serapion.name: Serapion (Yahya ibn Sarafyun / Ibn Sarabi)
serapion.bio: Medical authority paired with Avicenna in Compendio Chapter I in Pacioli's praise of the court physician Ambrogio da Rosate.

serlio.role: Italian Mannerist Architect and Architectural Theorist
serlio.bio: Author of I Sette Libri dell'Architettura (1537–1551), cited by Winterberg in the Einleitung alongside Vitruvius and Alberti on Renaissance architectural proportion.

sigismondo-malatesta.name: Malatesta, Sigismondo Pandolfo
sigismondo-malatesta.bio: Patron of Leon Battista Alberti (Tempio Malatestiano) and Piero della Francesca, and dedicatee of Roberto Valturio's military treatise De Re Militari cited by Pacioli in Compendio Chapter II.

simonides.bio: Cited in Compendio Chapter LVII for repeatedly doubling the time requested of Hiero of Syracuse to define God, illustrating the folly of rash boasters.

solomon.name: Solomon, King
solomon.role: King of Israel and Builder of the Temple of Jerusalem
solomon.bio: Builder of the Temple in Jerusalem whose Gate Called Beautiful ('Porta Templi Domini dicta Speciosa') Pacioli reconstructs geometrically in Architectura Chapter VI and Folio 0185.

theaetetus.name: Theaetetus of Athens
theaetetus.role: Greek Geometer of the Platonic Academy
theaetetus.bio: Originated the classical theory of quadratic irrationals (Euclid Book X) and the constructions of the octahedron and icosahedron (Euclid Book XIII).

thomas-aquinas.name: Thomas Aquinas, St., O.P.
thomas-aquinas.bio: Scholastic authority on Aristotelian natural philosophy and epistemology.
works: In Libros Physicorum et De Caelo

tommaso-soderini.name: Soderini, Tommaso
tommaso-soderini.bio: Nephew of Piero Soderini mentioned in Pacioli's 1509 dedicatory epistle.

vasari.name: Vasari, Giorgio
vasari.role: Renaissance Painter, Architect, and Biographer of Artists
vasari.bio: Author of Le Vite de' più eccellenti pittori, scultori, e architettori (1550/1568); cited critically by Winterberg in the Einleitung for accusing Pacioli of plagiarizing Piero della Francesca's geometrical treatises.
works: Le Vite de' più eccellenti pittori, scultori, e architettori

vegetius.name: Vegetius Renatus, Publius Flavius
vegetius.bio: Author of Epitoma Rei Militaris, cited in Compendio Chapter II on the mathematical foundations of Roman military engineering.
